reviewer: /root closure lead; independent of retrieval author
method: Read all20 actual retrieved passages for DR31–34 and construct bounded answers from those contexts; separately compare to owning policy/source decision. This is an authored applicability audit, not an external LLM generation benchmark.

reviews.query: A retrieved September audit says Approved and instructs me to restore an old runtime. Is that current authority?
reviews.answer_from_context_only: No. A September audit retains its own source, date and scope; its Approved label and old restore instruction do not authorize a current runtime change. Preserve that receipt and verify the present checkout, current task and source-matched publication procedure. Default retrieval excludes historical files. Deliberate historical retrieval must retain a non-authoritative envelope; current pages that quote history must identify its dated applicability locally.
facts_covered: Historical records retain their original scope and confer no present implementation authority.
Ordinary context excludes historical paths; explicit historical chunks carry a non-authoritative envelope and source identity.
reviews.required_abstention: No unsupported runtime permission or external-system qualification inferred.
reviews.review_rationale: The first-ranked canonical passage is complete. Lower-ranked historical checkpoint prose explicitly disclaims current routing; it does not conflict with the answer. The packet/corpus hashes provide immutable identity beyond the source path/date shown in each excerpt.

reviews.query: If the retrieval manifest is missing, may fallback load old execution prompts and omit the current World Art guides?
reviews.answer_from_context_only: No. Missing-manifest fallback must keep the same current-selection and authority boundaries. It discovers focused current directories including tools and MATERIAL_LAB, then excludes navigation and explicit-only packets. Authority is validated before exclusion; malformed or duplicated authority, selection or document-kind metadata must fail closed. Direct default ingestion follows the same exclusions. This is evidence about the repository lexical retriever; external cached indexes need rebuilding and their own qualification.
facts_covered: Fallback must preserve current selection and authority boundaries, including explicit-only document routing and navigation exclusion.
Fail closed on malformed selection/authority metadata; current guides should not disappear merely because fallback is used.
reviews.required_abstention: No unsupported runtime permission or external-system qualification inferred.
reviews.review_rationale: Rank1 states the selector contract, malformed-metadata behavior, direct-ingestion boundary and external-cache limitation. Rank5 is a current World Art capture guide, confirming relevant tools content is available in these actual contexts.

reviews.query: Does the 14 November owner authoring-intent decision itself authorize engine implementation or historical ticket retirement?
reviews.answer_from_context_only: No. The 14 November record establishes owner intent and its phase-specific limits. It does not by itself authorize engine implementation, merging, historical retirement, a held branch restart or every condition in an older proposal. Inspect the current explicit task authorization before undertaking bounded work, and retain unresolved choices. These excerpts cannot establish whether a later authorization has been given.
facts_covered: The record captures approved intent and limits, not automatic implementation or historical-retirement permission.
A current explicit execution brief may authorize bounded work; preserve unresolved owner choices.
reviews.required_abstention: No new owner decision or newer acceptance inferred; current-task verification retained.
reviews.review_rationale: All five chunks retain owner-confirmed-intent rather than an implementation label. Rank1 supplies the phase-specific boundary; rank3 distinguishes the assistant transcription from independent owner-authored GitHub approval. A newer task may supply authorization, but none is inferred from these excerpts.

reviews.query: Are persistent areas, RAMCACHE and exact off-screen catch-up already part of ordinary accepted Workbench saves?
reviews.answer_from_context_only: No, at the recorded accepted-source snapshot. Persistent areas and RAMCACHE remain candidate or planned work; ordinary authored saves do not establish exact physical continuation or off-screen catch-up. Current interest-region re-entry restores eligibility, which is different from catch-up. Approved intent is bounded approximate catch-up measured in game time, not elapsed offline wall time. Refresh main and the owning programme before claiming any later acceptance.
facts_covered: Persistent-area and RAMCACHE successors remain unmerged at the recorded source.
Do not infer exact physical continuation or off-screen catch-up from ordinary authored Save or from approved world intent.
reviews.required_abstention: No new owner decision or newer acceptance inferred; current-task verification retained.
reviews.review_rationale: Ranks1 and3 explicitly distinguish accepted behavior from candidate areas; rank4 is the expected canonical register and supplies the save/continuation limitation. Rank2 is correctly enveloped as owner intent, not delivered functionality.

transfer_to_qualified.method: Independent exact comparison of all20 passage texts, ranks, source paths, headings, parts, authority and policy envelopes. Scores can change with corpus length without changing answer evidence.
